question.text: If the complex numbers <math><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">sin</mi></mrow><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mi>i</mi><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">cos</mi></mrow><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow></mrow><mi mathvariant="normal"></mi></math> and <math><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">cos</mi></mrow><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>-</mo><mi>i</mi><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">sin</mi></mrow><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow></mrow></math> are conjugate of each other, then the number of values of <math><mi>x</mi></math> in the interval <math><mfenced open="[" separators="|"><mrow><mn>0,2</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow></mfenced></math> is equal to (where, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mi>i</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></math>)

solution.text:
sin⁡x=cos⁡x and cos⁡2x=sin⁡2x
⇒sin⁡x=cos⁡x & 2cos2x-1=2sin⁡xcos⁡x
⇒sin⁡x=cos⁡x & 2cos2x-1=2cos2x
⇒sin⁡x=cos⁡x & -1=0 (Which is impossible)
Hence, no value of x exists
